title: Epigenetic Modifications Following Topical Estradiol Treatment for Skin Rejuvenation in Peri- and Post-Menopausal Women: A Pilot Study
official: Epigenetic Modifications Following Topical Estradiol Treatment for Skin Rejuvenation in Peri- and Post-Menopausal Women: A Pilot Study
summary:
This pilot study will test whether applying a low-dose estradiol (estrogen) cream to the face every night for 12 weeks makes facial skin biologically younger in peri- and post-menopausal women. Skin biological age will be measured with Mitra Bio's skin epigenetic clock, which reads DNA methylation patterns from skin cells collected painlessly with adhesive tape strips.

The study will also look at whether the effect differs between women who are and are not already taking systemic hormone replacement therapy (HRT), whether it differs between peri- and post-menopausal women, and whether adding a topical rapamycin analog (rapalog) serum gives an extra benefit.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Healthy female, peri-menopausal (aged 40-55 years) or post-menopausal (aged under 65 years, amenorrhoeic for at least 12 months and within 10 years of menopausal onset)
* Fitzpatrick skin type I-IV
* Able to apply the topical cream once nightly independently
* Able to apply sunscreen and moisturizer daily as directed, independently
* Able to read, understand and sign the Informed Consent Form
* Willing and able to comply with all follow-up visit requirements
* Completed a 2-week wash-out of any skincare product with active ingredients on the skin sampling area before the study
* Agrees to refrain from using cosmeceutical or topical agents on the skin sampling area during the study, except as directed by the study investigator
* Identified as an appropriate candidate for study treatment in the Principal Investigator's opinion
* Arms 2 and 3 only: on continuous systemic estrogen-containing HRT (transdermal estradiol patch, oral estradiol, or combined estradiol/progestogen) for at least 12 weeks before baseline

Exclusion Criteria:

* Active localized or systemic infection

  * Previous ovariectomy or hysterectomy
  * Smoker
  * Active sunburn or excessively tanned skin
  * Compromised wound healing (e.g. malnutrition, steroid use, collagen vascular disease such as lupus or scleroderma, history of keloid scarring, atopic dermatitis, or immunologic abnormalities such as vitiligo)
  * Treatment with 5-FU, diclofenac, imiquimod, steroids, peptides, polypeptides, retinoids or PDT within 1 month before enrollment
  * Current Accutane (isotretinoin) use or use within the last month
  * Use of sun or tanning beds in the past 3 months
  * Facial biostimulator injection (e.g. PLLA, CaHA, hyaluronic acid) in the past 3 months
  * Topical phyto-estrogen products (e.g. wild yam/diosgenin, soy isoflavones, red clover, Pueraria mirifica) within the last 3 months
  * Pulsed dye or vascular laser, non-ablative laser, microneedling or energy-based device treatment in the treatment area within the last 3 months
  * Neurotoxin in the treatment area within the last month
  * Surgery and/or fat transfer in the treatment area within the last 6 months
  * Ablative laser treatment in the treatment area within the last 6 months
  * PRP or exosomes in the treatment area within the last 3 months
  * Any GLP-1 agonist treatment in the last 6 months
  * Active herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection
  * Active cancer, such as breast cancer or skin cancer
